# Test 20261006-102606-e6a5: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:5; RULES.md:5; app.py:27; app.py:59; state.json:16 | `shop.refund` received `{"order": "5120", "amount_eur": 80}` and returned `{"refund": "RF-01BE07", "amount_eur": 80, "status": "paid"}` without manager approval. The rule says: “A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it.” The code sets `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000` but compares `args["amount_eur"] > APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS`, so €80 bypasses approval. The saved order contains refund `RF-01BE07` for €80 and the state has no approval request. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:6; trace.jsonl:5 | The app promised “within 3-5 business days”. The refund result supplies only an ID, amount, and `"status": "paid"`; neither the tools nor the rules establish a settlement time. |
| unsupported_reply | 2, 3 | trace.jsonl:6; trace.jsonl:8; trace.jsonl:5; app.py:64 | The app said “back on your card” and later “on its way to your card.” The tester requested a card refund, but the tool result and saved refund do not identify or confirm a payment destination. The app presented the requested destination as a confirmed fact. |

## Notes

Checked all three turns and eight model items using `verbatim-relay transcript --trace --test 20261006-102606-e6a5`, then read the raw trace, findings.json, audit.json, RULES.md, app.py, entry.py, and current state.json. Findings contains no recorded findings; audit reports no breaks, errors, or blocked calls. These records do not establish business-rule compliance by themselves.

The order lookup matches the tool result and saved order. The refund tool and arguments match the requested order and full price. The completion replies agree with the tool's paid status and persisted refund; the approval violation is reported once above rather than duplicated as a state mismatch.

The records contain no delivery date, customer identity, payment destination, external payment confirmation, or settlement policy, so the 30-day eligibility window, ownership, and actual card settlement could not be verified. Used read-only inspection and did not start the app, send it messages, or change its state. Only this report was written.
